finding: Dense Q8_0 dp4a is only ~1.2x over the existing t16 GEMV at the verifier shape, NOT the 2-3x the 4-bit MoE dp4a achieved. Q8_0 is already int8 (1 byte/weight) so the dense GEMV is bandwidth-bound on the weight read; dp4a is a compute optimization and does not reduce bytes read. At rows=4 launch overhead also dominates the per-call wall. Conclusion: dp4a is the right lever for 4-bit MoE weights (#7, deferred) but NOT for dense Q8_0. The verifier wall is launch/dispatch-count-bound (ROOFLINE 5.3 hidden bucket) + bandwidth, not dense-GEMV compute. The real lever is launch-count reduction (kernel FUSION / graph replay), not per-kernel GPU dp4a.
decision: Keep the correct single-output q8_0 dp4a kernel (committed, validated) as a registered option, but do NOT pursue the full dual/triple-split + raw-Q8_0 materialization + dispatch integration -- poor ROI (1.2x, likely flat at the wall). Pivot to fusion.
